{{Short description|Statement in number theory}}
In [[number theory]], '''Li's criterion''' is a particular statement about the positivity of a certain sequence that is equivalent to the [[Riemann hypothesis]].  The criterion is named after Xian-Jin Li, who presented it in 1997. In 1999, [[Enrico Bombieri]] and [[Jeffrey C. Lagarias]] provided a generalization, showing that Li's  positivity condition applies to any collection of points that lie on the Re(''s'') = 1/2 axis.

==Definition==
The [[Riemann Xi function|Riemann {{math|''&xi;''}} function]] is given by
:<math>\xi (s)=\frac{1}{2}s(s-1) \pi^{-s/2} \Gamma \left(\frac{s}{2}\right) \zeta(s)</math>

where ζ is the [[Riemann zeta function]].  Consider the sequence

:<math>\lambda_n = \frac{1}{(n-1)!} \left. \frac{d^n}{ds^n} 
\left[s^{n-1} \log \xi(s) \right] \right|_{s=1}.</math>

Li's criterion is then the statement that

:''the Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to the statement that <math>\lambda_n > 0</math> for every positive integer <math>n</math>.''

The numbers <math>\lambda_n</math> (sometimes defined with a slightly different normalization) are called Keiper-Li coefficients or Li coefficients. They may also be expressed in terms of the non-trivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function:

:<math>\lambda_n=\sum_{\rho} \left[1- 
\left(1-\frac{1}{\rho}\right)^n\right]</math>

where the sum extends over ρ, the non-trivial zeros of the zeta function. This [[conditionally convergent]] sum should be understood in the sense that is usually used in number theory, namely, that

:<math>\sum_\rho = \lim_{N\to\infty} \sum_{|\operatorname{Im}(\rho)|\le N}.</math>

(Re(''s'') and Im(''s'') denote the real and imaginary parts of ''s'', respectively.)

The positivity of <math>\lambda_n</math> has been verified up to <math>n = 10^5</math> by direct computation.

==Proof==

Note that <math>\left|1-\frac{1}{\rho}\right| < 1 \Leftrightarrow |\rho-1| < |\rho| \Leftrightarrow Re(\rho) > 1/2</math>.

Then, starting with an entire function <math>f(s) = \prod_\rho{\left(1-\frac{s}{\rho}\right)}</math>, let <math>\phi(z) = f\left(\frac{1}{1-z}\right)</math>.

<math>\phi</math> vanishes when <math>\frac{1}{1-z} = \rho \Leftrightarrow z = 1-\frac{1}{\rho}</math>. Hence, <math>\frac{\phi'(z)}{\phi(z)}</math> is holomorphic on the [[unit disk]] <math>|z| < 1</math> iff <math>\left|1-\frac{1}{\rho}\right| \ge 1 \Leftrightarrow Re(\rho) \le 1/2</math>.

Write the [[Taylor series]] <math>\frac{\phi'(z)}{\phi(z)} = \sum_{n=0}^\infty c_n z^n </math>.  Since 
:<math>\log \phi(z) = \sum_\rho{ \log \left(1-\frac{1}{\rho (1-z)}\right)} = \sum_\rho{ \log\left(1-\frac{1}{\rho}-z\right)-\log(1-z)}</math> 
we have 
:<math>\frac{\phi'(z)}{\phi(z)} = \sum_\rho{ \frac{1}{1-z}-\frac{1}{1-\frac{1}{\rho}-z}}</math>
so that 
:<math>c_n = \sum_\rho{ 1-\left(1-\frac{1}{\rho}\right)^{-n-1}} = \sum_\rho {1-\left(1-\frac{1}{1-\rho}\right)^{n+1}}</math>. 
Finally, if each zero <math>\rho</math> comes paired with its [[complex conjugate]] <math>\bar{\rho}</math>, then we may combine terms to get 
{{NumBlk|:|<math>c_n = \sum_{\rho}{Re\left(1-\left(1-\frac{1}{1-\rho}\right)^{n+1}\right)}</math>.|{{EquationRef|1}}}}

The condition <math>Re(\rho) \le 1/2</math> then becomes equivalent to <math>\lim \sup_{n \to \infty} |c_n|^{1/n} \le 1</math>.  The right-hand side of ({{EquationNote|1}}) is obviously nonnegative when both <math>n \ge 0</math> and <math>\left|1-\frac{1}{1-\rho}\right| \le 1 \Leftrightarrow\left|1-\frac{1}{\rho}\right| \ge 1 \Leftrightarrow Re(\rho) \le 1/2</math> . Conversely, ordering the <math>\rho</math> by <math>\left|1-\frac{1}{1-\rho}\right|</math>, we see that the largest <math>\left|1-\frac{1}{1-\rho}\right|> 1</math> term (<math> \Leftrightarrow Re(\rho) > 1/2</math>) dominates the sum  as <math>n \to \infty</math>, and hence <math>c_n</math> becomes negative sometimes.
{{cite arXiv
 | author = P. Freitas
 | title = a Li–type criterion for zero–free half-planes of Riemann's zeta function
 | year = 2008
 | eprint =  math.MG/0507368
}}

==Generalizations==
Bombieri and Lagarias demonstrate that a similar criterion holds for any collection of [[complex number]]s, and is thus not restricted to the Riemann hypothesis.  More precisely, let ''R''&nbsp;=&nbsp;{''ρ''} be any collection of complex numbers ''ρ'', not containing ''ρ''&nbsp;=&nbsp;1, which satisfies

:<math>\sum_\rho \frac{1+\left|\operatorname{Re}(\rho)\right|}{(1+|\rho|)^2} < \infty.</math>

Then one may make several equivalent statements about such a set. One such statement is the following:

:''One has <math>\operatorname{Re}(\rho) \le 1/2</math> for every &rho; if and only if''
::<math>\sum_\rho\operatorname{Re}\left[1-\left(1-\frac{1}{\rho}\right)^{-n}\right]
\ge 0</math>
:''for all positive integers n''.

One may make a more interesting statement, if the set ''R'' obeys a certain [[functional equation]] under the replacement ''s''&nbsp;↦&nbsp;1&nbsp;&minus;&nbsp;''s''. Namely, if, whenever &rho; is in ''R'', then both the complex conjugate <math>\overline{\rho}</math> and <math>1-\rho</math> are in ''R'', then Li's criterion can be stated as:

:''One has'' Re(''&rho;'')&nbsp;=&nbsp;1/2 ''for every'' ''&rho;'' ''if and only if''

::<math>\sum_\rho\left[1-\left(1-\frac{1}{\rho}\right)^n \right] \ge 0</math>

:''for all positive integers n''.

Bombieri and Lagarias also show that Li's criterion follows from [[Weil's criterion]] for the Riemann hypothesis.

In 2006, P. Freitas proved that all of the zeros of the Riemann zeta function lie inside the region <math>\Re(s) \leq \tau/2 </math>, where <math> \tau \in [1/2, \infty) </math> [[if and only if]] the numbers
::<math> \sum_\rho\left[1-\left(\frac{\rho}{\rho-\tau}\right)^n \right] </math>
are non-negative for all positive integers <math> n </math>. These coefficients are called the ''<math>\tau </math>-Li coefficients''.<ref name="Fre2006">{{cite journal |last1=Freitas |first1=Pedro |title=A Li-type criterion for zero-free half planes of Riemann's zeta function |journal=J. London Math. Soc. |date=2006 |volume=73 |issue=2 |pages=399–414 |doi=10.1112/S0024610706022599 }}</ref> A. Droll<ref name="Droll2012">{{cite book |last1=Droll |first1=Andrew |title=Variations of Li's criterion for an extension of the Selberg class |date=2012 |url=https://qspace.library.queensu.ca/server/api/core/bitstreams/33e62268-c1f8-4b99-a987-ee2e7b13768f/content}}</ref> generalized the results to the extended [[Selberg class]], A. Bucur, A.-M. Ernvall-Hytönen, A. Odžak and L. Smajlović<ref name="BEHOS2016">{{cite journal |last1=Bucur |first1=Alina |last2=Ernvall-Hytönen |first2=Anne-Maria |last3=Odžak |first3=Almasa |last4=Smajlović |first4=Lejla |title=On a Li-type criterion for zero-free regions of certain Dirichlet series with real coefficients |journal=LMS J. Comput. Math. |date=2016 |volume=19 |issue=1 |pages=259–280 |doi=10.1112/S1461157016000115 }}</ref> investigated the behavior of the coefficients for certain functions violating the Riemann hypothesis, and N. Palojärvi<ref name="Pal2020">{{cite journal |last1=Palojärvi |first1=Neea |title=Explicit Zero-Free Regions and a τ -Li-type Criterion |journal=Albanian J. Math. |date=2020 |volume=14 |issue=1 |pages=47–77 |doi=10.51286/albjm/1608313766 |arxiv=1807.01506 }}</ref> proved explicit conditions between finitely many <math> \tau </math>-Li coefficients and zero-free regions.
